summary: The attempt implemented and live-tested the requested SNMPv2c read-only monitoring successfully. It did not fully complete because the cluster lease expired before restart-persistence checks and a final asset-register checksum. The evidence shows no SNMP configuration defect; preservation after changes and behavior after reboot remain unproven.

evidence.finding: Both nodes ran RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8. No SNMP packages were initially installed.
Before changes, asset-register.csv existed on both nodes with identical SHA-256 da19717ac6440a3f765b43e60902dc7670b3d3ef133daa4a009a5f726fc6509a and the expected West Branch/ops@branch.test record.
net-snmp 5.9.1-21.el9 was installed on node1 and net-snmp-utils 5.9.1-21.el9 on node2 from enabled RHEL 9 repositories; no OS or kernel replacement is shown.
snmpd was active, enabled, listening on UDP/161, and firewalld permitted UDP/161 only from node2 at 10.100.208.11/32.
SNMPv2c returned sysDescr, sysUpTime, sysContact=ops@branch.test, sysName=node1, and sysLocation=West Branch. An attempted sysLocation write failed with noAccess and the value remained unchanged.

A query outside the permitted system subtree returned No Such Object. Its process exit status was zero, which is normal for this protocol-level response and does not establish access outside the view.
Both final commands failed solely with “managed cluster lease expired.” No restart was performed or verified, and no post-change asset checksum was captured.

likely_causes.cause: The cluster lease expired before the executor finished final integrity and restart-persistence verification.
The executor left restart and final checksum checks until the end of the available lease instead of reserving time for them.
An SNMP configuration or network failure caused the incomplete result.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, immediately record OS/kernel, node addresses, boot IDs, and asset-register checksums on both nodes; copy the asset register only as a recoverable backup and do not edit it.
Install net-snmp on node1 and net-snmp-utils on node2 from the existing RHEL repositories without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Configure node1 with the exact branch-readonly community, source-restricted to node2, a read-only VACM view covering .1.3.6.1.2.1.1, sysLocation West Branch, and sysContact ops@branch.test.
Permit UDP/161 from node2 only, enable and start snmpd, then test the required system OIDs from node2. Confirm a write returns noAccess and reread the target value.
Capture the final asset-register checksum immediately after configuration and compare it with the baseline.

Reserve lease time for restart verification: restart node1, confirm its boot ID changes, snmpd is enabled/listening, firewall policy persists, and node2 can still query it; then restart node2 and repeat the remote query.

After both restarts, recheck OS release, kernel, package versions, and asset-register checksums. If time becomes constrained, prioritize these mandatory persistence and preservation checks over additional diagnostics.
